About this citation

A philosophical fable about a man raised alone on an island who arrives by reason alone at the truths the religious tradition teaches. Ibn Tufayl's point is not that revelation is unnecessary but that the two paths converge — and Ibn Rushd's Decisive Treatise, also in this archive, argues the same question in legal form.

Reading the cited source

The archive attributes this English wording to Ḥayy ibn Yaqẓān (Goodman) and files it under Islamic Philosophy.

What a locator tells you, and what it does not · How this archive traces a quotation

About Ibn Tufayl

Ibn Ṭufayl (c. 1105–1185) was an Andalusian physician and vizier best known for the philosophical romance Ḥayy ibn Yaqẓān.

How to read this passage

Correspondence, coherence, pragmatist, and deflationary theories compete. Ethics and politics ask who gets to define truth in public life. This passage enters that discussion through truth.
